fixes.explanation: That's it, baker. Jesus says, "I know your deeds; you are neither cold nor hot." Then He adds, "How I wish you were one or the other!" (Revelation 3:15)

Yep. That's a strong picture. He says, "So because you are lukewarm—neither hot nor cold—I am about to vomit you out of My mouth!" I think this is one of those lines you read once and sit with for a minute. It's heavy, and it comes right after He says He wishes they were hot or cold.

Not this time, baker. Jesus never says alone in this part. He says they don't realize they are "…wretched, pitiful, poor, blind, and naked." Alone isn't the word, and later in this letter He's the One standing at a door and knocking.

A pearl of great value shows up in one of Jesus' parables (Matthew 13:46), but not here. In this letter He counsels them to buy "…gold refined by fire so that you may become rich…" So the shopping list has gold on it, not pearls.
True, friend. Jesus says they are "blind," and then counsels them to buy "…salve to anoint your eyes so that you may see." He doesn't just name the problem. He offers the fix.
Close to the mood, but that's not what He says. Jesus says, "Those I love I rebuke and discipline." Forgetting Him isn't mentioned in this verse. Love is who He names.
Not this time, baker. Jesus says, "If anyone hears My voice and opens the door, I will come in…" He says anyone, and He doesn't say only leaders. So it's anyone who hears Him and opens the door.
That's the one, friend. Jesus says, "…I will come in and dine with him, and he with Me." He comes inside to share a meal with them. I love that, because a meal is where people really stay a while.

That one doesn't show up here, friend. Jesus speaks of the new Jerusalem in His letter to the church in Philadelphia (Revelation 3:12). Here, to the one who overcomes, He says, "…I will grant the right to sit with Me on My throne…" So the throne is the promise in this letter.
